label: Exponential improvement continuing
rationale: The best 80% METR time horizon reached 32.3 min (GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, Nov 2025), growing at a ~7-month doubling rate long-run and possibly ~4 months in 2024–2025. Caveat: METR's RCT found experienced developers 19% slower with AI tools, so benchmark gains do not yet translate to real-world productivity.

label: Approaching
rationale: No verified case meets the strict criteria (solo founder, $10M ARR, <10 hrs/week oversight); Magnific AI is at $10M ARR with 2 people and several AI-heavy solo founders are at ~$3M ARR. Current examples show AI as a coding accelerator, not an autonomous business operator.

label: Distant
rationale: The largest confirmed AI-generated patch merged into Linux is ~50 lines (in 6.15, undisclosed and buggy), 200× short of the 10k-line target. Major projects (Gentoo, NetBSD, Git, QEMU) ban or restrict AI code, and AI is adopted only in auxiliary maintenance roles.

label: Distant (structurally blocked)
rationale: All major journals (Nature, Science, Cell, JAMA/Lancet/BMJ) prohibit AI authorship, so the barrier is policy and accountability rather than capability. The closest approach, Sakana AI Scientist-v2's ICLR workshop paper, was accepted and then withdrawn.

label: Ahead: 80% horizon 185.9 min (Apr 2026); doubling ~4.1 mo in 2 yrs vs ~7 mo benchmark (tier 3)
rationale: The release-cohort METR 80% time horizon rose from 4.42 min (frontier at 2024-09-30) to 185.91 min (Claude Mythos Preview early, released 2026-04-07), a 42x gain over the 2-year window across 9 new frontier points: a log-linear fit gives a doubling time of 4.1 months (95% CI 3.4-5.1), and the endpoint ratio gives 4.45 months. That beats the tier-3 benchmark of sustaining METR's long-run ~7-month doubling, and it is faster than the previous window 2022-09-30..2024-09-30 (0.26 -> 4.42 min, endpoint doubling 5.9 months), so the status is green (Ahead). The result survives dropping the latest, wide-CI point (4.4 months), and it already absorbs the ~6 months since April 2026 with no new frontier.

basis.rule: KPI green: the window trend moves in the goal direction (up) at >= the benchmark pace (doubling time <= ~7 months)
basis.assessed_quantity: metr-80-horizon-by-release: highest METR 80%-success time horizon (minutes) among models released on or before each date (METR-Horizon-v1.1 results file); goal_direction up

current.robustness: without the 2026-04-07 point (CI 97-398 min): OLS 4.40 mo, endpoint 5.52 mo

window.change: window doubling time 4.1-4.5 months (current) vs 5.9 months endpoint (previous): faster, clearly beyond noise
window.method: frontier points = dated 'new p80 frontier' rows (the monthly 'as of' duplicate rows 2025-04/08/11 excluded); OLS of log2(minutes) on months; endpoint = frontier at window end vs start
window.source: uv run ledger.py series robots-software metr-80-horizon-by-release --as-of 2026-09-30

basis.benchmark: Tier 3 (own long-run trend): sustain the long-run doubling time of ~7 months; observed 4.1 mo (OLS) / 4.45 mo (endpoint) over 2024-09-30..2026-09-30
basis.benchmark_source: METR (Kwa et al. 2025) long-run doubling time (event 2025-03-19-metr-long-tasks-doubling-rv: ~7-month doubling over six years)
basis.data_as_of: 2026-04-07 (latest frontier point; METR results file retrieved 2026-09-28 shows no later frontier; cadence 'irregular' with no registered release lag, so not flagged stale)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays green. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-kpi) used the non-bound label 'Exponential improvement continuing' and scored the legacy as-evaluated series (metr-80-horizon-frontier, 32.3 min) rather than the registered release-cohort series metr-80-horizon-by-release. It compared no current vs previous window, cited no benchmark tier, and mixed in quantities that are not the assessed metric (SWE-bench, the METR developer RCT). Its '~4-month' figure came from a claim that re-verification removed. Under v1 the 2-year window doubling time of ~4.1 months beats the tier-3 ~7-month benchmark, so the status is green (Ahead).

label: Progressing: solo AI-heavy firms ~$3-3.5M ARR; <10 h/week oversight unevidenced; ETA 5-10 yrs
rationale: No verified achievement event shows a single-person company at $10M ARR with <10 hours/week of oversight. The closest solo cases are about $3M (Pieter Levels, corrected record) and Base44's $3.5M ARR before its $80M exit (legacy); the $10M-plus small-team cases are 2-person Magnific or the largely pre-AI 1-person BuiltWith (legacy, non-primary), with no oversight data. That is measurable progress on the revenue half at ~1/3 of the target, and OpenView finds AI-native startups 8x likelier to reach $10M ARR within 12 months, but nothing evidences the <10 h/week clause, and there is no programme or non-proponent corroboration that would support a <=5-year ETA. The credible ETA is 5-10 years, so the status is yellow.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity (solo-company ARR) with a credible ETA of 5-10 years; not green (no funded programme, precursor at relevant scale or non-proponent corroboration of the oversight clause); not achieved (no verified achievement event)
basis.eta: 5-10 years (~2031-2036): solo ARR at ~$3-3.5M needs ~3x, and the <10 h/week oversight clause has no evidenced precursor
basis.path: AI-leveraged solo businesses (Pieter Levels ~$3M revenue; Base44 $3.5M ARR, legacy) and tiny AI teams at $10M ARR (Magnific, 2 people, legacy); AI-native startups 8x likelier to reach $10M ARR in 12 months (OpenView)
blockers: Technical/operational: no evidence of any company at this revenue run with <10 h/week of human oversight (reliability/agency of autonomous operation)
Data: revenue and headcount figures are self-reported or secondary (LinkedIn, tinyteams), and oversight hours are never reported
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays yellow. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-milestone-the-10m-solopreneur) used the non-bound label 'Approaching' and judged proximity rather than an ETA. It gave no ETA, path or blockers basis, and it cited records since superseded: the Levels figure was corrected from '$3.1M ARR' to about $3M revenue, and the OpenView record was re-verified. Under v1 yellow rests on measurable ARR progress with a 5-10 year ETA; the unevidenced oversight clause rules out green.

label: Distant: one LLM-written patch merged (Linux 6.15, human-submitted); no path to a 10k-line AI patch
rationale: The only verified precursor is LWN's report that a patch merged for Linux 6.15 was entirely LLM-written and posted without disclosure; re-verification removed the earlier size and bug details, and it was human-submitted. There is no series on the size of accepted AI-generated patches to extrapolate and no funded programme aiming at AI-submitted large patches. Torvalds positions AI for maintaining, not writing, kernel code, and critical-infra projects ban AI code (Gentoo, QEMU) or require a human in the loop (LLVM), which cuts against an 'AI-submitted' patch. With no evidenced path, the status is red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: no evidenced path (no series on the milestone's own quantity and no programme or precursor at relevant scale), so the ETA is not evidenced within 10 years
basis.eta: >10 years / not evidenced: a single small, human-submitted LLM-written patch is the only precursor, and there is no trend on accepted AI-patch size to extrapolate
basis.path: None evidenced. Precursor: undisclosed fully LLM-written patch merged in Linux 6.15 (LWN, Jun 2025). Context (legacy): kernel TAB 'generated-content' disclosure guidelines proposed Nov 2025; Levin's RFC for AI-assistant config files, Jul 2025
blockers: Policy: Gentoo and QEMU bar AI-generated contributions and NetBSD bans them (legacy); LLVM requires a human in the loop, which conflicts with an 'AI-submitted' patch
Social/process: maintainers position AI for maintenance rather than authorship (Torvalds, Dec 2025); 10k-line diffs face heavy review burden
Definitional: 'AI-submitted' excludes the human-submitted AI-written patches that are the only precursors
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays red. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-milestone-the-linux-kernel-patch) scored the distance to goal ('~50 lines, 200x short of 10k'), which STATUS.md reports but never scores. The ~50-line and 'buggy' details it relied on were removed on re-verification. It gave no ETA, path or blockers basis, and it cited records since superseded (Gentoo, QEMU, Torvalds, LWN). Under v1 red rests on the absence of any evidenced path (Distant), with the policy obstacles named.

label: Blocked: Nature/Science bar AI authorship (policy); best precursor an ICLR workshop paper, withdrawn
rationale: The milestone requires AI credited as primary author in Nature/Science, and both journals' policies bar AI authorship: 'LLMs do not currently satisfy our authorship criteria' and 'AI tools cannot be authors' (legacy record, used as context). That is a structural policy block whatever the technical readiness. The best verified precursor is Sakana's AI Scientist-v2 paper, which passed peer review at an ICLR 2025 workshop but was withdrawn before publication because the community had not decided whether to publish AI-generated manuscripts. Recognitions such as the 2024 chemistry Nobel went to humans, so no evidence moves the block, and the status is red (Blocked).

basis.rule: Milestone red: structurally blocked (policy: the target journals prohibit AI authorship), whatever the technical readiness
basis.eta: >10 years / blocked: it cannot happen until Nature or Science changes its authorship policy, and no evidence shows such a change underway
basis.path: Technical precursor only: AI Scientist-v2 paper passed peer review at an ICLR 2025 workshop, then was withdrawn (Sakana, Mar 2025). Context: 36% of cancer-paper abstracts AI-generated with 9% disclosure (legacy), i.e. AI contributes uncredited
blockers: Policy: Nature Portfolio and Science/AAAS (plus Cell, ICMJE journals) prohibit crediting AI as an author (legacy record)
Policy/community: the only peer-reviewed fully AI-generated paper was withdrawn because the community has not decided whether to publish such work
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays red. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-milestone-the-nature-author) used the label 'Distant (structurally blocked)', but when the reason is structural v1 calls for 'Blocked' with the block named and typed. It misstated the Sakana withdrawal as 'per a prior ethical agreement' (corrected: withdrawn under the experiment protocol because the community is undecided) and cited records since superseded (Sakana, AlphaFold Nobel). It also gave no ETA, path or blockers basis.
